reviews: [★5] Incredible 5G performance at budget price - The MediaTek Dimensity 6300 chip handles daily multitasking, YouTube streaming, and casual gaming without any noticeable heat or lag.
[★5] Smooth 120Hz display - The high refresh rate makes scrolling through Instagram and Reddit silky smooth, especially impressive for a smartphone under 12k.
[★5] Excellent battery life - 5000 mAh battery easily lasts full day and a half on moderate use with 6-7 hours of screen-on-time.
[★5] Attractive Amber Gold finish - The feather textured back panel looks distinct and does not catch ugly fingerprint smudges.
[★5] 50MP AI primary camera - Captures vibrant daytime photos with balanced sharpness and natural skin tones.
[★4] Decent secondary camera - Ultra-wide lens is absent, but the main shooter is very capable for outdoor portraits.
[★4] Fast 15W charging - Takes around 90 minutes to fully charge the phone from 15%, which is reasonable for this price category.
[★4] Clean UI with minimal bloat - Realme UI 5.0 on Android 14 is responsive, though some glance lockscreen notifications require disabling.
[★4] Great speaker volume - Single bottom speaker is loud and crisp for watching videos and taking speakerphone calls.
[★4] Reliable side fingerprint sensor - Unlocks device instantaneously on light tap without fail.
[★5] Fantastic value for money - You get solid 5G bands, 120Hz display, and 128GB storage at a very competitive price.
[★5] IP54 splash resistance - Gives peace of mind during light rainy season commutes.
[★5] Premium in-hand feel - Slim 7.89mm profile makes it comfortable to use one-handed.
[★5] Clear voice calls - Dual microphone setup does a great job filtering background traffic noise on Airtel and Jio.
[★4] Good signal stability - Connects to 5G NSA and SA networks reliably with fast download speeds.
[★4] Dedicated MicroSD slot - Nice to have expandable storage alongside dual physical nano SIM cards.
[★3] Average low light camera - Night mode photos can appear slightly grainy when lighting is very poor.
[★3] Plastic frame - Build is entirely polycarbonate, though expected for this segment.
[★3] Vibration motor is basic - Haptic feedback is a bit buzzy rather than subtle.
[★4] Smooth gaming in BGMI - Runs smoothly on smooth/ultra settings with consistent 40-45 fps.
[★5] Best budget 5G phone - Recommended for students and parents looking for reliable everyday performance.
[★5] Very good display brightness - 625 nits peak brightness is easily legible under outdoor shade.
[★4] Responsive touch sampling - 240Hz touch sampling rate feels snappy when typing fast.
[★4] Sturdy build quality - Dropped once from waist height with the bundled TPU case, zero damage.
[★5] Quick delivery by Flipkart - Received within 24 hours with secure open-box delivery.
[★4] Decent selfie camera - 8MP front shooter takes clean photos in good lighting.
[★3] Charging adapter not super fast - Wish they had included 33W charging like older Narzo models.
[★4] Lightweight design - Weighs under 190 grams and feels balanced in trouser pockets.
[★5] Overall top contender - One of the best 5G phones you can buy under 12,000 INR.
[★4] Solid daily performer - No complaints after 3 weeks of continuous usage.
